newsitem.title: USA: Ex-N.Y. cop pleads guilty to assault on policewoman.
newsitem.headline: Ex-N.Y. cop pleads guilty to assault on policewoman.

text.p: A former New York City police officer, wounded in 1994 by a fellow officer in a friendly fire shooting, pleaded guilty Tuesday in a separate case to assaulting a policewoman.
Desmond Robinson entered the plea to avoid facing attempted rape charges in the case.
Robinson, 33, was alleged to have attempted to rape a female officer in Manhattan last May after a night of heavy drinking, prosecutors said.
The victim, who appeared in Criminal Court in Manhattan, strenuously objected to the deal worked out between prosecutors and the former police officer.
She asked Manhattan Crimimal Court Judge Laura Visacion-Lewis to reject the plea bargain deal and have the case presented to a grand jury.
"I believe this is a sick and troubled person who I befriended for some time," the female officer said. "It is extremely important that he acknowledge what he has done to me and to apologise."
She described how she and Robinson had become close friends when she served as his counsellor while he recuperated from his bullet wounds.

Robinson, who is black, was shot four times in 1994 on a crowded subway platform by a white off-duty officer who mistook him for a suspect. Robinson was working undercover and not wearing a uniform at the time in a case that touched off a controversy over police procedures and race relations.
Robinson was ordered to undergo counselling and to have no contact with the victim or her family for three years.
